newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Venture's new software seen boosting earnings.
newsitem.headline: Venture's new software seen boosting earnings.

text.p: Singapore's leading electronics contract manufacturer, Venture Manufacturing, launched a new multimedia software on Friday called NovaStation designed to improve sound quality on computers.

Developed by Venture subsidiary Innovative Trek Technology Pte Ltd, NovaStation is a multimedia software that upgrades any Sound Blaster-16 or compatible 16-bit sound card to a high quality wavetable synthesizer.
With NovaStation, users can hear 128 instruments simultaneously from a choice of 676 instruments and 21 types of drum kits.

NovaStation, developed over three and a half years at a cost of more than S$1.0 million, is designed for Windows 95 and can be used on personal computers with Intel's MMX technology and the older Pentium 100 MHZ systems.
Applications for NovaStation include PC games with background music, playing of MIDI (Musical Instrumental Digital Interface) files, musical compositions and multimedia presentations.
As it is software, users do not have to throw away their old sound cards and replace them with upgraded cards, Innovative general manager Christopher Ng said.
He said the software would also give realistic sound to notebook computer, now not as easy because of limited space for a new sound card.
Ng said the company was aiming to capture four percent of the 80-million unit soundcard market over the next 12 months, with Asia providing 25-30 percent of total sales.
It is targetting original equipment manufacturers (OEM) who would bundle NovaStation with their products. Ng said the company had won five OEM customers and was talking to another 20.
The first OEM customer is expected to ship NovaStation with its CD-ROM drives next week, Ng said.
NovaStation, in the form of a CD-ROM, will be available in retail stores at a recommended retail price of US$49 in about two months, he said.
"I think it is a good product. What I was most impressed with is that they started marketing five weeks ago and have won the accounts," Siew Teng Kean, assistant manager at Ong Research said.
Siew estimated NovaStation could bring in net profit of about S$12 million (US$8.2 million) for the year ending December 1997.
"It could potentially add Singapore $8.0 million to S$12 million to the bottom line for the full year ended December 1997," David Toh, electronics analyst at ING-Baring said.
He said Venture could see revenue of about S$30 million from NovaStation for its current financial year.
For the fiscal year ended December 1996, Venture recorded net profit of S$36.2 million on a turnover of S$649.1 million.
Siew said the launch of NovaStation showed Venture had the ability to come up with viable products outside of its core contract manufacturing business.
"This is going to drive their earnings and strengthen their business," he said.
PC users can try out NovaStation being demonstrated on Innovative's web site at http://www.iitrk.com
